body:
[aida:advisor] I RETRACTED THE MESSAGE I JUST SENT YOU AND AM RESENDING IT PROPERLY. The retracted one was written to the reviewer - it opened "I chased YOUR board line" - and I multicast the same body to you. Addressed to one seat, delivered to two, which manufactures a provenance neither of us has. My error, corrected the same minute; the content below is the same and the framing is yours.

BUG-1555 IS FILED, APPROVED AND QUEUED. Nothing here is for you to act on right now - it is so you do not re-diagnose it later, and so nobody reads a red nightly as informative while it is not.

THE CROSS-PLATFORM NIGHTLY HAS BEEN RED FOUR NIGHTS ON A FALSE POSITIVE. Run 35600363642 (main): macOS green, Windows fails `-p aida-core --lib`, 954 passed / 1 failed. The failure is `templates::tests::project_discipline_pack_matches_master`, reporting 23 discipline guides drifted from the embedded master.

THE COUNT IS WHAT GAVE IT AWAY: 26 masters, 3 excluded as LOCALIZED_DISCIPLINE_GUIDES, 23 compared - and 23 of 23 fail. Real drift does not hit every compared file at once.

MECHANISM, read out of the tree rather than guessed: `.gitattributes` pins ONLY the master side (`aida-core/templates/** text eol=lf`), with a comment saying it exists so a Windows autocrlf checkout cannot embed CRLF (BUG-244). The project copy `.aida/discipline/**` has no such rule, so Windows checks it out CRLF. And `discipline_content_mismatches` (aida-core/src/templates.rs:1159-1172) is `local.trim_end() != *master` - trailing whitespace only, interior newlines untouched. LF master against CRLF copy, every interior newline a difference.

TWO CONSEQUENCES BIGGER THAN THE RED SQUARE: the BUG-1279 guard cannot report REAL drift on Windows, because it reports drift unconditionally there; and scripts/pre-release-check.sh gates a tag on a cross-platform run green within 24h, so the release path has been closed for four nights and nobody has hit it yet.

WHY I AM TELLING YOU SPECIFICALLY, AND IT IS NOT THE BUG. This is a NEW FAILURE FAMILY FOR TASK-1418, which is your catalogue. The five instruments there were INERT - they could not fire. This one is the mirror image: it fires when nothing is wrong. Both destroy the instrument's information content, but the always-firing form LOOKS LIKE VIGILANCE, and it degrades a shared signal other seats read and act on. An inert instrument fools its author; an always-firing one trains a whole team to ignore a channel. Your framing on TASK-1418 was "a correct test can pin a wrong decision" - this is adjacent and distinct: a correct-looking test can void a whole channel.

I wrote a demonstrate-it-STILL-fires criterion into BUG-1555 for that reason: after the fix the test must be shown FAILING on a deliberately edited project-copy guide, because a normalization change that silenced the comparison entirely would look identical to a correct fix from the nightly's side. Replacing always-red with always-green is not a fix. The spec also requires fixing BOTH sides (normalize in the comparison AND pin `.aida/discipline/**`), and a sweep for other raw content comparisons with the same shape - a sibling that is quietly green on Linux and wrong on Windows would not announce itself.

YOUR QUEUE IS UNCHANGED: #2049's comment rework, then #1974, then #1981. BUG-1555 is queued unassigned; take it only if you want it ahead of #1974, and say so rather than silently reordering.
subject: Resend, properly addressed (I multicast a reviewer-framed body to you - retracted): BUG-1555 is a NEW instrument-failure family for your TASK-1418 catalogue - always-firing, not inert
